summary: This bill amends the Higher Education Act to bar federally funded colleges from taking adverse actions like discipline, funding cuts, or derecognition against students or single-sex social organizations solely because of their single-sex membership rules, while allowing colleges to enforce other conduct standards.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the Higher Education Act to add association protections for students in single-sex social organizations at institutions receiving federal funds. It imposes no new appropriations, spending mandates, or cuts, and does not alter any funding levels or programs.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue measures of any kind.
The bill contains no references to health insurance, medical care delivery, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
No content relates to firearms, background checks, restrictions, or Second Amendment protections.
The legislation does not mention visas, borders, pathways to citizenship, or enforcement.
No language addresses reproductive rights, access to abortion services, or restrictions thereon.
No provisions concern defense budgets, military funding, or national security expenditures.
The bill does not engage with environmental regulations, emissions standards, or conservation policies.
No references to welfare programs, food assistance, Medicaid, or other safety-net entitlements appear.

While the bill amends the Higher Education Act and applies to federally funded colleges, it addresses only student freedom-of-association rules for single-sex social organizations. It neither increases public-school funding nor promotes school choice or privatization, so it does not engage the defined poles of this topic.
No provisions relate to controlled substances, decriminalization, or enforcement practices.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal procedure.
No content concerns tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization measures.
The legislation neither authorizes deficit spending nor directs resources toward debt reduction.
The bill protects single-sex (biological-sex) membership practices under Title IX but contains no language expanding or limiting legal protections specifically for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions address foreign assistance, international aid programs, or related funding.
The bill does not touch on voting access, voter ID, election administration, or campaign rules.
No sections address data privacy, technology regulation, or surveillance oversight.
The legislation does not engage with collective bargaining, worker protections, or union rights.
The bill protects freedom of association for single-sex organizations and references Title IX but does not create or modify religious exemptions or balance them against anti-discrimination rules.
